summary: Serving mix observed during gradual rollout: subset of prod requests routed to pinned legacy model due to stale route cache
description:
Issue summary:
Customer noticed inconsistent outputs after we began a staged rollout (canary -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%) for gptj-13b-v2. A portion of traffic that should have been served by the new pinned variant is still being routed to the legacy pinned version, leading to quality regressions for some API calls.

Impact:
- BrightShop reported ~12% of requests in prod (us-east-1) returned responses that match the legacy model profile (longer responses, different tokenization) causing downstream classification mismatch and user-visible correctness regressions.
- Customer is on a Dedicated plan with pinned model versions; this is blocking their scheduled go-live for the new variant.

Environment:
- prod | us-east-1 | Dedicated pool id: ded-45
- Affected endpoints: /v1/chat/stream, /v1/generate (token streaming observed)

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Client pins model via route header X-Model-Pin: redwood/gptj-13b-v2:2026-03-01
2) Deploy rollout policy in Console: canary 10% -> 25% -> 50%
3) Observe traffic in their analytics and compare response signatures for a stable test prompt set

Observed behavior:
- Intermittent routing to legacy model variant despite policy showing canary served by new variant.
- Traces show route decision entry using new variant, but downstream serving node returns legacy model id in response metadata.
- Route cache TTLs were set at 30s cluster-wide; some nodes reported last cache sync >90s behind.

Expected behavior:
- During rollout, route decisions for a request should consistently and atomically pick the variant specified by the rollout policy for that request, and downstream serving nodes should honor the decision (no mixed-model responses for a single request/trace).

Logs/traces (excerpt):
- Trace ID: trace-e12f3b - decision_layer: variant=new_v2, route_cache_version=317
- Serving node: node-12 - response_metadata.model_id=redwood/gptj-13b-v1:2025-10-20
- Router logs: WARN "route cache miss" node=node-12 last_sync=2026-03-12T09:21:02Z

Temporary mitigation applied:
- Support requested a manual cache invalidation for affected pool ded-45 and a rolling restart of routing-proxies in us-east-1. Early telemetry shows legacy-routed percentage dropped from ~12% to ~1.5% immediately after invalidation.

Investigation notes:
- Hypothesis 1: stale per-node route cache caused earlier routing decisions recorded in traces to mismatch with serving node cached model mapping.
- Hypothesis 2: race between rollout configuration propagation and local cache TTL expiry; when rollout policy changed, some nodes didn't apply new policy before serving in-flight requests.
- Confirmed: some routing-proxy instances had not picked up the new config (last successful config pull older than rollout start).
- Correlation: nodes with older kernel version (serving-runtime v3.4.2) more likely to miss invalidation hooks; v3.4.6 shows correct behavior.

Next steps / action items:
- SRE: complete rolling restart of routing-proxies in ded-45 to force config sync (in progress).
- Eng (serving-runtime): backport a deterministic route cache invalidation fix (PR linked). Expect targeted patch to reduce window to <5s.
- Support/CS: schedule a short maintenance window with customer for final cutover once patch is deployed.

Customer communication plan:
- Sent immediate mitigation note and asked for permission to proceed with rolling restarts.
- Planned follow-up: provide post-deploy verification script and ask customer to run their prompt set to confirm 0% legacy responses.
